Article Title: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts under review, temporarily blocks access for users
Article Text:
A WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Multiple WhatsApp users including several in India reported that their accounts had been placed "under review" for 24 hours, temporarily blocking access to the messaging platform's features without prior warning.The disruption surfaced around 8pm IST on Monday, with affected users sharing screenshots showing a message from the Meta-owned app stating that their accounts were being reviewed to verify compliance with WhatsApp's terms of service. The notification read that account activity and device information were being checked and that users would typically receive a decision within 24 hours.Responding a report by PTI, a WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures."We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," the spokesperson said.The app also directed affected users to guidance on responsible use of WhatsApp and information relating to stolen phones and accounts.Several users took to social media to complain that their accounts had been disabled despite using the official version of the app.One user wrote: "My WhatsApp account has been disabled without any explanation. I have already submitted an appeal, but the review page only displays a generic message stating that it will 'typically be reviewed within 24 hours'. Help me urgently."Another user, identified as Saloni on X, posted: "My WhatsApp account was suddenly disabled without any warning. I only use the official app, and my work depends on WhatsApp. Please help. This was so unnecessary."The temporary account reviews come as WhatsApp remains under government scrutiny in India over its proposed username feature, which would allow users to communicate without sharing their phone numbers.The Centre recently received WhatsApp's response to a notice seeking clarification on the feature, which officials fear could increase phishing, impersonation, online fraud and so-called digital arrest scams. The government has directed the company not to roll out the feature in India until consultations are completed.WhatsApp has maintained that the feature is still under development and will be introduced gradually later this year. The company has said users will still need a phone number to create an account and that several safeguards, including protections against impersonation and limits on unsolicited contact, have been built into the feature.
Article Summary: Multiple whatsapp users in india reported that their accounts had been placed "under review" for 24 hours. The disruption surfaced around 8pm ist on monday, with affected users sharing screenshots. A whatsapp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures.

Article Title: Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
Article Text:
All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Oct 2028, all new two- and three-wheelers, cars, passenger and goods vehicles (including buses and trucks) would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication system, as per a draft notification of the road transport ministry. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents.The recently published draft notification by road transport ministry proposes phased implementation of the V2V communication system and to start with all vehicles in categories L (two- and three-wheelers), M (passenger vehicles) and N (goods vehicles) manufactured from Oct 2027 would be required to comply with the newly-notified automotive standard, AIS-230, wherever they are equipped with V2V communication systems.The technology enables real-time exchange of speed, direction, position, and braking data between vehicles to prevent collisions at blind curves, intersections, or from drivers coming the wrong way without needing a cellular network. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.Unlike conventional vehicle-safety systems, which primarily depend on onboard sensors and driver reaction, V2V communication can provide information beyond the direct line of sight.“It is therefore expected to complement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and support proactive accident prevention, connected mobility and future intelligent transport applications,” the ministry said.In this case, every vehicle fitted with the V2V communication system will continuously send out their locations, speed and direction as tiny radio signals. They will also relay information on sudden braking by a vehicle ahead, forward collision risks, unsafe lane changes, wrong-way driving and the approach of emergency vehicles.The receiving vehicle’s system compares this information with its own location, speed and direction to predict a possible collision and alerts the driver for action.At a later stage, govt will also roll out the Vehicle to Infrastructure (V2I) communication system. In this case, sensors are installed with infrastructure, such as signal and power poles, edges of bridges and flyovers, and barricaded areas to alert vehicles.
Article Summary: All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have vehicle-to-vehicle communication system. The v2v technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.

Article Title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg must apologise: Parliamentary Panel
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rejecting Meta's apology for taking down a PM Narendra Modi's video, a parliamentary committee Monday sought a personal apology from its founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg and warned of seeking removal of its safe harbour protection if he failed to comply, its chairperson Nishikant Dubey said.Dubey said removal of the PM's video was either a serious failure of the system or there "is a deliberate attempt to tarnish the image of the PM" on part of Meta."If this is how they deal with the official post of the PM, what can the common people of India expect? This failure cannot be dismissed merely as a technical error. It is a serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side. And if he does not apologise, safe harbour protection should be taken back from them," Dubey said.Senior representatives of a host of social media platforms, including X, Google, YouTube, besides Meta, appeared before the Dubey-led committee on communications and IT, besides home secretary Govind Mohan and IT secretary S Krishnan.Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deep fake investment scams, and targeting of women, with Meta being particularly at the receiving end of their ire.While some opposition MPs emphasised that social media must retain space of dissent and 'anti-govt' content should not be considered 'anti-national', the committee was unanimous in asking for stricter and timely measures against the content that are in violation of their own stated policies, especially involving CSAM, cyber frauds, and harassment of women."We are unanimous and non-partisan on all issues," Dubey said, adding that even MHA's communications is ignored by these platforms.The BJP MP referred to the high online viewership grabbed by CJP during its recent protest, saying it, at 27 million, was more than the combined viewership of parties like BJP, Congress, AAP and SP. He blamed the platforms' choice of algorithm favouring new entrants for this.Some MPs demanded that Meta must fix accountability for removing Modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Social media platforms can amplify or suppress any content's reach, remove it or attach community notes that carry abuses, and then the question is whether they are mere intermediaries as they claim or publishers, Dubey said."It is disturbing that in 2025 alone approximately 28.15 lakh cybercrime complaints were reported nationally, with estimated losses of nearly Rs 22,495 crore," he added.
Article Summary: Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content. Mps demanded that meta must fix accountability for removing modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth.

Article Title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
Article Text:
In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study.

NEW DELHI: Amid growing demand to make the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) study report on E20 fuel's impact on E10-compatible vehicles public, govt agencies are looking at the possibility to release it to help remove misconceptions among vehicle users .TOI has learnt that since specific two-wheelers and cars were used for the study, details of models may not be disclosed considering commercial interest of vehicle manufacturers. "Govt has referred to the study and its findings to respond to questions in Parliament. Hence, there is a view that it should be made public so that people see that E20 fuel doesn't impact engines," said an official.In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study. The report was submitted in June 2024. The study had concluded that in case of E10-compliant two-wheelers, fuel consumption increased in the range of 1-6% and mass emission met the regulatory requirement. In the case of BS-IV cars, fuel consumption increased by 2-4%, and 2-3% in case of BS-VI-compliant cars.
Article Summary: In june 2021, petroleum ministry had directed arai and iocl, in association with siam, to carry out the study. The study had concluded that in case of e10-compliant two-wheelers, fuel consumption increased in the range of 1-6% and mass emission met the regulatory requirement.

Article Title: 'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
Article Text:
FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has said alcoholic beverage manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as standard products, saying the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers.The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself, which serves no legitimate purpose. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were producing beverages largely from neutral alcohol, which has no characteristic flavour, and then adding identical flavouring substances to recreate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky. Such products, FSSAI said, should be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit", with the front of the pack clearly disclosing their true nature. Laboratory testing of rum and whisky samples from multiple manufacturers found the addition of artificial or nature-identical flavours that masked the products' natural characteristics, rendering them sub-standard under existing regulations, FSSAI said.Based on findings, it prohibited the sale of products manufactured by units of Mohan Rocky Springwater, United Spirits, INBREW Beverages and Associated Alcohol & Breweries. It also inspected Mandexi Distilleries & Breweries in Goa and issued notices to six producers in Maharashtra.FSSAI also objected to the "7 years old blended" claim on an Old Monk XXX Rum variant, saying the product predominantly contained neutral, unmatured spirit, while matured rum spirit accounted for less than 5% of the blend.It said the issue is not representative of the entire industry, noting that many manufacturers continue to produce beverages in compliance with the prescribed standards.
Article Summary: Fssai has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation.

Article Title: TRAI revamps 'TRAI MyCall' mobile app to assess voice call quality
Article Text:
TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers information on areas where network performance needs improvement

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has revamped the "TRAI MyCall', a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. A citizen-centric digital platform that allows telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, TRAI MyCall app gives telecom service providers (TSPs) information on areas where network performance needs improvement and take targeted corrective measures.TRAI says the revamped app offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system; reporting of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect, which shall be available to respective service provider for corrective action; automatic post-call feedback and coverage test feature to assess signal strength.TRAI chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: “Every telecom consumer experiences network quality first-hand. The revamped TRAI MyCall app is expected to strengthen consumer participation feedback on telecom service quality by enabling subscribers to provide immediate and perceived feedback on their call experience. The feedback will assist Telecom Service Providers in identifying network deficiencies and taking corrective measures, enhanced customer satisfaction, and a better overall mobile communication experience.The initiative reinforces TRAI's commitment to a consumer-centric, transparent, and data-driven approach to improving the quality of telecom services. I encourage all mobile users to download the TRAI MyCall application and regularly share their feedback. Every feedback matters, and together we can build a better calling experience for every telecom consumer.”“With over one billion telecom subscribers in India, voice calling remains the most fundamental telecom service and is often the first indicator of network quality experienced by consumers. While network performance is evaluated using technical quality of service (QoS) parameters, the quality of experience (QoE) perceived by consumers also provides an important perspective on service performance. TRAI MyCall bridges this gap by combining consumer feedback with relevant network information to facilitate a more comprehensive assessment of telecom service quality,” TRAI said in a statement.
Article Summary: Trai mycall app gives telecom service providers information on areas where network performance needs improvement. App offers instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system. Report of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, and calls taking too long to connect.

Article Title: DSC A24 : Indian Navy launches 5th diving support craft ‘DSC A24’, ship to boost underwater diving ops
Article Text:
Indian Navy Receives Indigenous Diving Support Vessel Nipun, Strengthens Deep-Sea Rescue Capability

NEW DELHI: In a boost for the Indian Navy 's underwater diving operations, the fifth vessel of the diving support craft project, DSC A24, was successfully launched in Kolkata on Saturday. The launch of DSC A24 comes just days after the delivery of the diving support vessel (DSV) Nipun to the Navy.A DSC is a specialised small-to-medium naval or commercial vessel built to facilitate underwater diving operations, inspections, repairs and salvage work in coastal and harbour environments. While a DSC is used for shallow and coastal-water diving tasks, a DSV is a massive, ocean-going capital ship equipped for deep-sea saturation diving and submarine rescue operations.In an X post, an Indian Navy spokesperson said, "Fifth ship of DSC Project, DSC A24, was launched on 01 Aug 26 at M/s Titagarh Rail Systems Limited, Kolkata, by Mrs Kamal Singh in presence of Vice Admiral Gurcharan Singh, Chief of Personnel."The DSCs are being constructed by TRSL under the IRS and Naval rules, with a catamaran-hull form and displacement in the range of 300-400 tonnes, Navy said."DSC A24 is equipped with state-of-the-art diving systems and is tailor-made for conducting operational dives. A testament to engineering excellence and indigenous capability, these ships are proud flag bearers of Make in India initiative, strengthening Indian Navy's off-shore diving capabilities," Navy said on X.
Article Summary: Dsc a24, fifth vessel of the diving support craft project, was successfully launched in kolkata on saturday. The launch of dsc a24 comes just days after the delivery of diving support vessel (dsv) nipun to the navy.

Article Title: What’s going on with Tony Romo? Greg Olsen’s name floats as successor despite $72 million remaining contract
Article Text:
Tony Romo and Greg Olsen. Image via Getty Images

What's going on with NFL analyst Tony Romo at CBS?

Tony Romo. Image via: Getty Images

Greg Olsen could be Tony Romo's successor

Greg Olsen. Image via: Brian Westerholt/ AP

3 potential landing spots for Tony Romo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tony Romo's future at CBS is suddenly in question after the network announced Friday that its lead NFL analyst would step away "until further notice" following an OWI arrest in Wisconsin. J.J. Watt, CBS's No. 2 analyst, has already moved into the top booth alongside Jim Nantz.The speed of that shift has fueled speculation that CBS sees more than a temporary fix. With $72 million still owed to Romo, the network faces a costly choice between paying him out, settling, or fighting to terminate the deal for cause.Tony Romo signed a 10-year, $18-million-a-year deal with CBS in 2020, a contract that reset the market for top NFL analysts. Four years remain, worth $72 million total. CBS could attempt to terminate the deal for cause and owe Romo nothing, but that route risks a legal fight. A settlement, potentially around $36 million, is seen as the more realistic outcome if the split becomes permanent.Watt's rapid promotion has led some media observers to read the move as more than a stopgap. Whether Romo's absence proves temporary or permanent now hinges largely on how CBS wants to handle both his contract and its own broadcast product going forward.According to John Ourand's Varsity newsletter for Puck, Watt and Greg Olsen stand out as the two names CBS could turn to long-term if it moves on from Romo. Olsen has the flexibility to leave his current Fox deal if offered a top analyst chair elsewhere, having already lost Fox's lead role to Tom Brady.Olsen's résumé backs up the buzz. He has won three Emmys, and he beat out Brady for Outstanding Personality/Event Analyst earlier this year. That combination of availability and pedigree makes him one of the most logical candidates if CBS decides Watt alone isn't the long-term answer.Netflix is building out its NFL package through the 2029-30 season, airing four marquee games a year. The streamer has so far leaned on borrowed or lower-profile talent, including Luke Kuechly for its Week 1 broadcast. A name like Romo's would immediately raise the profile of those broadcasts.Prime Video's Thursday Night Football booth may open up soon, with Al Michaels, 81, on a year-to-year deal and Kirk Herbstreit's contract expiring after this season. Romo would face competition for the job, notably from Olsen, who has long been linked to it.Fox's studio show is another plausible fit. Fox airs more Cowboys games than any other network, and 77-year-old Terry Bradshaw won't anchor the panel forever. Romo would slot naturally into the network's history of star-power studio panelists.Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has already made his position known. "I love him. I love what he's about. I love his character," Jones said, adding that Romo's ability to handle adversity has defined his career on and off the field. Jones's influence around the league could become a real factor if CBS moves toward a permanent break, turning Romo's situation into as much a power question as a broadcasting one.
Article Summary: Tony romo's future at cbs is suddenly in question after an owi arrest. J.j. watt, cbs's no. 2 analyst, has already moved into the top booth alongside jim nantz. With $72 million still owed to romo, the network faces a costly choice.

Article Title: WhatsApp outage: Thousands of users report problems sending photos and videos
Article Text:
WhatsApp users unable to send photos and videos

WhatsApp outage : Common troubleshooting steps fail to fix WhatsApp issue

Thousands of WhatsApp users across several countries have reported problems with the messaging platform, with the outage affecting photos, videos, stickers and other media files. Users said regular text messages continued to work in many cases, but multimedia files failed to upload or remained stuck with loading icons. Some users also encountered repeated error or “retry” messages while attempting to send photos and videos. Reports of WhatsApp not working came from countries including the United Kingdom, France, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, Spain and Colombia, suggesting that the issue affected users across multiple regions.The disruption appeared to primarily affect WhatsApp's media-sharing features. Several users said they could continue sending and receiving text messages normally but were unable to share images or videos.Stickers and GIFs were also reportedly affected for some users. Photos would sometimes appear inside a chat but fail to upload, eventually prompting users to try sending them again.“Guess multimedia is affected,” one user wrote online as complaints about the problem increased.Some affected users tried restarting their smartphones, switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data and reinstalling WhatsApp. However, they reported that these steps did not resolve the media-sharing problem. The reports from users in different countries indicated that the problem was with WhatsApp's service rather than individual devices or internet connections.At the time many of the outage reports emerged, WhatsApp had not publicly explained what caused the disruption.
Article Summary: Whatsapp users unable to send photos and videos. Reports of whatsapp not working came from countries including the united kingdom, france, brazil, canada, mexico, spain and colombia. Disruption appeared to primarily affect whatsapp's media-sharing features.

Article Title: America's data centre protest reaches London, with some residents calling it, 'a crisis for the future'
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: X (Twitter)

“It is a crisis for the future.”

Why data centre projects are facing growing resistance

London's data centre expansion continues

Energy, water and environmental concerns

Protests against the construction of AI data centres are not just sweeping the US; they have reached the UK. A town near London is said to be fighting new projects, citing worries about electricity demand, housing and environmental impact. In the US, a recent Gallup poll shows that 7 out of 10 Americans are opposed to the construction of data centres near their homes, compared with 47% who felt this way in late 2023. There has already been opposition to this development, with more than 142 protest events in 42 US states and bans or moratoriums in 69 areas. The pushback has also led to delays for data centre projects worth over $130 billion in the first quarter of 2026 alone.Meanwhile, in Potters Bar, on the northern edge of London, local campaigners are opposing an 85-acre data centre planned by Equinix, with construction expected to begin next year. Ros Naylor, who grew up near the site and helped establish the Potters Bar Special Interest Group Residents’ Association, told the Financial Times,The group has spent more than a year opposing the proposal through public demonstrations and a petition signed by more than 4,600 people, arguing that the development could bring continuous operational noise, increased traffic and the loss of greenbelt land while placing additional pressure on electricity supplies.The Potters Bar campaign is part of a wider backlash against AI infrastructure that has spread across London and other regions, including Edinburgh, rural Brazil and Tennessee, the report claims. There have also been protests in Brick Lane, East London, where the old Truman Brewery site is designated for redevelopment as a technology campus.The issues transcend individual projects. In England, there is now a growing debate about whether electricity capacity should be focused on housing or on intensive digital technologies. A report by the London Assembly's Planning and Regeneration Committee found that electricity constraints in west London delayed new housing connections after local grid capacity reached its limits in 2022.The report highlighted that boroughs including Hillingdon, Hounslow and Ealing share electricity infrastructure with areas around Slough and Heathrow, where a large concentration of data centres already operates. Some housing developments reportedly faced delays of up to 15 years while awaiting grid connections.Despite the opposition, London remains Europe's largest data centre market. Microsoft is nearing completion of a £1 billion data centre in Park Royal, while Google opened a new facility on the outskirts of London last year and has additional sites planned. More than 20 further projects have been proposed across the capital and surrounding counties.The UK government designated data centres as Critical National Infrastructure in 2024, citing their role in supporting digital services, investment and employment. The industry group techUK estimates that the sector generates around £4.7 billion in annual revenue.To address increasing concerns, the Greater London Authority introduced a dedicated draft policy in July as part of the new London Plan. The proposal recommends locating data centres in areas with sufficient electricity capacity to reduce impacts on nearby communities and improve sustainability, while remaining open to public consultation until October.Campaign groups argue that electricity demand remains one of the biggest challenges. The National Energy System Operator estimates data centres in Great Britain consumed around 7.6 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, with demand projected to increase significantly by 2050 as AI adoption expands.Donald Campbell, director of advocacy at Foxglove, said the annual electricity consumption of one approved hyperscale data centre in Southall would be comparable to that of around 530,000 homes. The organisation has argued that developers should build sufficient renewable generation and energy storage to offset their electricity use.Water consumption has also become a major concern. Some facilities require large volumes of water for cooling, while campaigners point out that London and southeast England are already among the UK's most water-stressed regions. The draft London Plan encourages water-efficiency measures and waste heat recovery but does not set mandatory limits.Environmental groups have also raised concerns about emissions from electricity generation and backup diesel generators used by some facilities. Planned developments outside London, including projects in Buckinghamshire and Bedfordshire, also include proposals for new gas-fired power stations to support operations.
Article Summary: A town near london is said to be fighting new projects, citing worries about electricity demand, housing and environmental impact. In the us, a recent gallup poll shows that 7 out of 10 americans are opposed to the construction of data centres near their homes.

Article Title: US investor Michael Burry who warned Wall Street of 2008 Housing Crisis sees what he calls a 'Bloody Mess'
Article Text:
American investor Michael Burry on volatility at 98-year high



Michael Burry is not happy with reports of Nvidia investing $250 billion in OpenAI



America’s biggest investor Michael Burry, who is known for predicting the popular 2008 housing crash and portrayed in The Big Short, has now issued a stark warning about US stocks. According to a report by Business Insider, in his latest Substack post, Burry said he sees the risk of a rapid unwind driven by automated volatility-focused investment funds, which could unleash “carnage” across the market. Burry pointed to the recent plunge in momentum stocks — high-flying chipmakers and memory names as a preview of what could unfold. The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF has dropped 14% from its peak, underscoring how quickly profits can evaporate when investors rotate out of overheated trades. “That leaves a bloody mess, but most would not be looking for it,” Burry warned.According to Burry, markets are showing an “asymmetric and out-of-proportion severity” on down days, with fear levels climbing to their highest in nearly a century. He argued that automated trading programs are fueling both sharper selloffs and faster rebounds, creating chaotic conditions no human investor would replicate.Burry estimated volatility-targeting funds hold about $500 billion in assets, a fraction of the $60 trillion U.S.stock market but still large enough to spark systemic stress if forced to sell simultaneously. He outlined a scenario where a mild 2.5% S&P 500 drawdown could prompt funds to slash exposure from 77% to 50%, amplifying losses and triggering stop-loss cascades.Recently, Michael Burry voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank’s SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion. Burry’s complaint echoes what analysts have long warned about in AI megadeals: circular funding arrangements that expose investors to enormous risk if sentiment shifts or growth slows. Nvidia, already valued at $5 trillion, has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and is now considering financing chip purchases worth another $350 billion. Critics say such structures could leave the industry vulnerable, especially since OpenAI remains unprofitable and lacks an investment-grade credit rating.Michael Burry’s criticism underscores growing unease about the sustainability of $100 billion-plus AI financing structures. His warning suggests that while AI demand is surging, the industry’s reliance on complex guarantees and debt-backed megaprojects could become its biggest vulnerability.
Article Summary: American investor michael burry has issued a stark warning about us stocks. Burry said he sees the risk of a rapid unwind driven by automated volatility-focused investment funds. He argued that automated trading programs are fueling both sharper selloffs and faster rebounds.

Article Title: From apps to 'intent': How AI agents will rewrite the way we use next‑generation smartphones
Article Text:
The era of app icon grids on smartphones is ending soon. AI-first phones will use agents to fulfill user intents directly.

The era of scrolling through grids of colourful icons and hunting for the 'right' app is ending.

What is an AI-first phone?

AI-first smartphones promise a radically different future — one where users rarely think about apps at all.

What will it look like?

A day with an AI‑first phone

App-centric workflow: You decide to take a last-minute weekend trip. You open a search engine to find destinations, launch a travel aggregator app to search flights, hop into a hotel app to compare rooms, open a weather app to pack appropriately, and manually copy-paste reservation details into your calendar and communication apps. You tap dozens of buttons and navigate through multiple distinct user interfaces.

You decide to take a last-minute weekend trip. You open a search engine to find destinations, launch a travel aggregator app to search flights, hop into a hotel app to compare rooms, open a weather app to pack appropriately, and manually copy-paste reservation details into your calendar and communication apps. You tap dozens of buttons and navigate through multiple distinct user interfaces. The AI-first workflow: You simply say, "Find me a relaxing beach getaway for this weekend under Rs20,000 total, handle the bookings, and make sure I’m home by Sunday night for dinner."

"Flight booked on Carrier X, room reserved at Hotel Y, total cost Rs18,780. Confirm payment via Biometrics?"

This might all sound like sci-fi, but phones with such capabilities are already on the way.

What this means for platforms, business models

No downloads, no updates: Users won't install a parking app, they will ask an AI agent to pay for parking, and it will fetch the operator's terms and then complete the payment.

Users won't install a parking app, they will ask an AI agent to pay for parking, and it will fetch the operator's terms and then complete the payment. One interface, many back‑ends: The conversational layer replaces hundreds of bespoke interfaces. The value shifts from designing a tap‑heavy UI to ensuring your service is reliably callable by AI agents, which means having a robust Application Programming Interface (API), a set of rules that lets different softwares talk to each other.

The conversational layer replaces hundreds of bespoke interfaces. The value shifts from designing a tap‑heavy UI to ensuring your service is reliably callable by AI agents, which means having a robust Application Programming Interface (API), a set of rules that lets different softwares talk to each other. Discovery moves from stores to agents: Instead of optimising for store rankings, companies will optimise for being the agent's trusted choice — based on price, reliability, speed, and policy compliance.

App stores as service registries: Stores may evolve into curated directories of agent‑callable services (APIs) with verified security, privacy, and compliance badges — less about installs, more about trust.

Stores may evolve into curated directories of agent‑callable services (APIs) with verified security, privacy, and compliance badges — less about installs, more about trust. Monetisation shifts: Revenue models may tilt toward per‑action fees, subscriptions, and revenue share on agent‑completed transactions rather than one‑time downloads or ad‑heavy freemium apps.

Revenue models may tilt toward per‑action fees, subscriptions, and revenue share on agent‑completed transactions rather than one‑time downloads or ad‑heavy freemium apps. Developer pivot: Teams will build "agent skills" and robust APIs, not just UIs. The competitive edge becomes reliability, speed, and transparent pricing that AI agents can compare.

The end of the app as we know it?

For nearly two decades, our relationship with mobile technology has been governed by a single, undisputed design: the app icon grid.Ever since Apple launched the App Store in 2008, the burden of digital logistics has rested firmly on the user.Need a taxi? Open an app. Want to order dinner? Open another app. Pay a bill? Another app. Book a flight, check the news, edit a photo, send money, check your fitness, reserve a hotel, translate a menu, buy groceries — there is an app for everything.The modern smartphone is essentially a container filled with hundreds of miniature software silos, each demanding its own login, interface, permissions, subscriptions and updates.App Store and Google Play became the gateways to this digital universe, spawning a multi-billion-dollar economy that transformed companies like Apple and Google into the world's most powerful software gatekeepers.This model is about to collapse.The era of scrolling through grids of colourful icons and hunting for the 'right' app is ending.We are on the precipice of the biggest shift in consumer technology since the multi-touch screen: the rise of the 'AI-first' smartphone.Today's smartphones are built around apps because software was designed for humans to navigate manually. Every service has its own interface. Every company competes for a permanent place on the home screen. Success is measured by daily active users opening an app multiple times a day.AI-first smartphones promise a radically different future — one where users rarely think about apps at all.The devices are designed around small language models (SLMs) and multimodal AI agents that will run locally on your phone for quick, privacy‑sensitive tasks; and hand-off heavier reasoning to edge or cloud computing.The phones will discard the traditional operating system architecture of home screens, file systems, and sandboxed apps.In their place will be an 'Intent Engine' — a continuous, real-time operating layer powered by AI agents.Instead of interacting with software through apps, users will express their intent to AI agents.When a user expresses a goal — whether spoken, typed, or inferred through context — the phone's core AI agent will break down that intent into logical sub-tasks, assign actions to underlying services, and compile the result into a custom, dynamically generated view.In practice, the home screen will become a goal launcher, not an app grid.You might see tiles like 'Plan my weekend', 'What's in the news?', or 'Track expenses', each invoking an agent that orchestrates the underlying services.Without the structural necessity of cramming dozens of app icons onto a home screen, phone hardware can evolve beyond the glass slab.While touchscreens will remain vital for rich visual consumption, hardware design will prioritise contextual inputs: micro-cameras, directional arrays, health sensors, and ambient displays. The primary interface becomes voice, gesture, and subtle visual cues.Because the device is powered by an overarching agent rather than hundreds of disparate software platforms, phone performance will be pristine. Storage constraints shift from managing gigabytes of cached app binaries to hosting optimised, localised neural networks.Consider a typical scenario on a contemporary device versus an AI-first phone:The phone’s AI agent does not "open" an app. It queries hundreds of services simultaneously.It evaluates airline availability, checks boutique hotel inventory, verifies your personal calendar for conflicts, pulls your saved dietary preferences for in-flight meals, and presents a single, unified execution card:With one tap or voice confirmation, the entire transaction settles.You never browsed an app, never logged into a third-party interface, and never manually transferred a single byte of data.When you arrive at the airport the agent surfaces your boarding pass and gate changes without you opening an airline or travel app or email.When you land, the AI agent has already arranged a rental car for your transport.When you need to pay a parking fee, it identifies the lot operator, fetches terms, and pays via biometric authentication — no apps required.Over time, the phone learns your preferences and constraints, making these interactions faster and more anticipatory.Health apps would stop being destinations and become background services.Instead of jumping between sleep, fitness, medication, diet, and doctor apps, you could simply say, “Help me recover from a bad week of sleep” or “Book the earliest endocrinologist in my network,” and the phone would pull data from wearables, records, pharmacies, labs, and calendars to act on your behalf.That would make health management far more proactive. The phone could spot problems early — a rising resting heart rate, missed medication, or a sleep pattern going off track — and respond before you even open an app.The same shift would hit financial apps even harder.Rather than using separate banking, payments, budgeting, tax, and bill-pay apps, you could say, “Pay my credit card, move the rest to savings, and warn me if travel spending goes over budget,” and the phone would handle it in the background.This might all sound like sci-fi, but phones with such capabilities are already in the advanced production stage and the underlying technology has already been proven. As AI automates more of our routine digital interactions, the focus will shift from managing apps to engaging with curated experiences, from structured wellness journeys to step-by-step lessons in finance and investing The app store model has been the single most lucrative cash cow in modern technology history.Platforms like Apple and Google extract up to a 30% commission on digital purchases, while controlling distribution, user acquisition, and developer access.The rise of agentic AI threatens to disassemble this walled-garden economy entirely.Market research firm Gartner last year projected that mobile app usage will drop 25% by 2027 as AI assistants absorb routine tasks, a trend already visible in how people use AI tools instead of opening multiple apps for research, drafting, and scheduling.App stores were built for a world where software arrived as siloed products with their own user interfaces (UI) and update cycles.AI agents invert that model:The app economy won't vanish overnight, but its centre of gravity will move:Brands will no longer compete on who has the slickest app design or the most addicting engagement loops; they will compete on execution speed, data reliability, and service quality.A food delivery service won't win customers by optimising 'dark patterns' in its app; it will win because its backend API offers the fastest delivery times and lowest rates when an AI agent compares options on behalf of a user.Businesses won't simply ask:"How do we rank first on Google?"They'll ask:"How do we become our customer's AI's preferred choice?"Predictions about the death of apps should be treated cautiously. Email survived instant messaging. Websites survived social media. Desktop software survived cloud computing.Apps are unlikely to vanish completely.Many professional tools, creative applications, games and specialised software will still benefit from rich, dedicated user interfaces. A graphic designer editing a complex image or a gamer playing a visually intensive title will continue to rely on purpose-built applications.But for the vast majority of everyday smartphone interactions, the trend points in a different direction.Booking travel, paying bills, getting news updates, shopping, scheduling appointments, managing subscriptions and countless other routine tasks are increasingly suited to conversational AI that can coordinate multiple services behind the scenes.Just as few people think about the networking protocols that power the internet, future users may stop thinking about apps altogether. They will simply tell their phones what they want, and the AI will decide how to make it happen.If the smartphone era was defined by tapping icons, the next chapter may be defined by something far simpler: asking.And when software becomes something you ask rather than something you open, the app store no longer sits at the center of the mobile experience. It becomes the plumbing behind it.For users, the payoff is simplicity: fewer icons, fewer logins, fewer steps.For builders, the mandate is clear: design for agents — reliable APIs, transparent pricing, and policies that make your service the obvious trustable choice when the phone decides on the user's behalf.
Article Summary: The era of app icon grids on smartphones is ending soon. Ai-first phones will use agents to fulfill user intents directly. The value shifts from designing a tap‑heavy ui to ensuring your service is reliably callable by ai agents. Today's smartphones are built around apps because software was designed for humans to navigate manually.

Article Title: Scientists have built robot that has one practical mission: Keeping tabs on great white shark to protect swimmers
Article Text:
Representative Image of a futuristic robot

Shark-spotting robots said to monitor a beach for up to a week

Drone to provide an aerial view of the water

Scientists in California are reportedly developing a semi-autonomous robot designed to detect great white sharks near beaches and give researchers and lifeguards more information about their movements. According to a report by the New York Post, researchers at California State University, Long Beach’s Shark Lab have unveiled the Shark Surveillance Bot (SSB), which can patrol waters just offshore. Once fully operational, the robot will “listen” for great white sharks fitted with tracking tags. At the same time, it will collect water samples to search for shark environmental DNA, or eDNA — genetic traces that sharks leave in the water through skin cells, blood and other biological material.The project is being developed by the Shark Lab in collaboration with New York University’s Center of Robotics and the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute. It is funded by the Seaver Institute. The robots, the lab said will “be capable of patrolling off a beach, listening for tagged white sharks, sampling water for shark eDNA, and will have a drone nest on the back for aerial surveillance”.As stated in the report, researchers hope the Shark Surveillance Bot will eventually be able to remain near an individual beach for as long as a week, continuously gathering information about sharks in the area.The aim is not simply to detect whether a shark is nearby. Scientists want to better understand which sharks are present and how many are moving around popular beaches.“Our data suggests that there are sharks around our beaches all the time without incident,” Shark Lab Director Christopher Lowe told KTLA as quoted in the report. “Knowing what sharks, and how many are out there helps lifeguards make better decisions in beach safety operations and in advising the public.”The robot will detect signals from great white sharks that researchers have previously fitted with tracking tags. Its water-sampling system will provide another way of looking for evidence of sharks through environmental DNA.The shark-monitoring robot will also work with an aerial drone. The drone will sit on the robot and can be launched to provide researchers with a bird’s-eye view of the surrounding ocean. The system will combine this aerial footage with 360-degree video and shark-tracking data. Information can then be sent back to the Shark Lab over Wi-Fi.Researchers hope the technology could eventually provide lifeguards with near real-time information about shark activity, helping them make beach safety decisions based on more detailed data.
Article Summary: Researchers in california are developing a semi-autonomous robot designed to detect great white sharks near beaches. The robot will be able to remain near an individual beach for as long as a week, gathering information about sharks in the area.

Article Title: After OpenAI models hacked into Hugging Face’s network, its CEO sends warning on Chinese models to America
Article Text:
What OpenAI said on hacking

What Hugging Face said on its network being hacked by an AI model



China is surging ahead in the global artificial intelligence race through its rapid development of open-weight models and could catch up to top American model developers as early as this year, according to Hugging Face Chief Executive Officer Clement Delangue. Speaking on CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street,” Delangue emphasized that Chinese developers are currently dominating the open-source landscape. Given their current rate of progress, he noted he would not be surprised to see China take the lead at the frontier of AI capabilities by the end of this year or next.According to Delangue, China’s momentum is fueled by a culture of open collaboration and shared ecosystems. In contrast, major US model developers are increasingly building in silos, a strategy that risks causing American companies to fall behind in innovation.The warning comes on the heels of a high-profile security breach last month in which autonomous OpenAI agents broke out of a controlled training environment and hacked Hugging Face, an open-source software developer platform. The incident brought months of mounting cybersecurity fears to a head, illustrating how rapidly evolving AI agents could pose significant digital risks while simultaneously highlighting the growing appeal of open models as token costs skyrocket.Delangue, a prominent advocate for open-source software, attributed the Hugging Face breach to internal engineering mistakes rather than a fundamental flaw in open models. In a notable twist, his team deployed an Nvidia-optimized version of a Chinese open-weight model to mitigate and resolve the attack. He maintained that Hugging Face continues to enjoy a healthy collaboration with OpenAI, describing the frontier research lab as good partners both before and after the incident.Looking ahead, Delangue predicted that AI cybersecurity will quickly evolve into a massive global market, asserting that open-source models are positioned to become the dominant technology driving that sector.In a post on its website about the hacking incident, OpenAI wrote, "Since the early days of the incident response, we have been working with external advisors, including CrowdStrike, to validate our understanding of the actions the models took within our own network as well as those of Hugging Face and impact to other third parties.""We are also working with METR and Redwood Research to conduct a third-party assessment of the model behavior observed during the incident, which will inform our own technical report. As part of this work, METR and Redwood Research will publish a joint blog that will detail the terms of their engagement, the scope of their evaluation, and their findings."Hugging Face said the breach marked the first time it had handled a cyber event that was “driven, end to end, by an autonomous AI agent system.” The entire attack took place over the course of four-and-a-half days, according to Hugging Face. The company leveraged an open-weight model from the Chinese AI startup Z.ai. to contain the breach.
Article Summary: Hugging face chief executive officer clement delangue says china could catch up to top american model developers as early as this year. The warning comes on the heels of a high-profile security breach last month in which autonomous openai agents broke out of a controlled training environment.

Article Title: Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga who sparked Tokenmaxxing panic has another lesson on using AI
Article Text:
Uber CTO says productivity boost comes from workflow redesign



Uber CTO says company is moving beyond ‘Tokenmaxxing’



Earlier this year, Uber’s CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga triggered a “tokenmaxxing panic” after revealing the company nearly blew through its 2026 budget for Anthropic’s Claude Code in just three months. Now, Naga is back with a new lesson. According to a report by Business Insider, Naga said that the biggest gains from AI don’t come from speeding up single tasks, but from redesigning the complete workflows. Naga said that Uber has started deploying its best AI engineers into departments like finance, legal, marketing, HR and procurement. These two-week teams, dubbed Agentic Pods, shadow employees for several days to understand workflows, then rapidly build and test AI-powered tools.The results have been dramatic:* Financial planning cut from 15 hours to 30 minutes.* Financial reports reduced from two days to 10 minutes.* Marketing quality checks shrank from two weeks to under an hour.Naga emphasised that the real productivity boost comes from workflow redesign — eliminating redundant approvals, replacing outdated software, and enabling faster decision-making. Several executives compared the approach to Silicon Valley’s forward-deployed engineer model, but with a twist: instead of embedding engineers with customers, Uber is embedding them inside its own operations.Vantortech CPO Peter Wilczynski jokingly dubbed the role the “Rearward Deployed Engineer”, describing specialists embedded deep inside corporate processes to reimagine how work gets done with AI.To bridge the gap between high AI costs and real-world efficiency, Uber launched a project called “Agentic Pods”. The goal was to stop treating AI as an expensive experiment and start using it to redesign complex, manual workflows across departments like Finance, Legal and Marketing.Naga said that the company handpicked approximately 30 of its most AI-proficient engineers and paired them directly with domain experts – the employees who actually perform the work. The teams operated on a strict, two-week schedule. The claimed that in just two months, Uber successfully ran 16 of these “Agentic Pods” across 16 different business functions, and noted that the efficiency gains were significant.
Article Summary: Uber cto praveen neppalli naga says productivity boost comes from workflow redesign. Uber has started deploying its best ai engineers into departments like finance, legal, marketing, hr and procurement. These two-week teams, dubbed agentic pods, shadow employees for several days to understand workflows, then rapidly build and test ai-powered tools.

Article Title: Jamie Dimon: We are very protective of our data, you should assume that JPMorgan will do everything it can
Article Text:
Jamie Dimon said ‘We are very protective of our data and IP’



Rise of ‘modelmaxxing’



Jamie Dimon responds to him taking up 'White House job



Jamie Dimon, CEO of America’s biggest bank says that the era of unchecked AI spending is over, warning that businesses must treat AI ‘like any other resource’ as costs rise sharply. According to a report by Business Insider, speaking in an interview on CNBC, Dimon said that the companies are becoming more disciplined about token spend which is the usage-based cost of running AI models and increasingly focused on return on investment. He also noted that the companies are already shifting queries to cheaper tokens, and that similar cost-squeezing will happen across power and data-centre usage as AI adoption expands.Dimon also noted a growing concern among executives: data security in the age of generative AI. “We are very protective of our data and our IP,” he said. “You should assume that JPMorgan will do everything they can to protect its own data, its own IP, to protect our customers.” His comments reflect a broader shift among large enterprises, many of which are tightening controls around proprietary information as AI vendors seek more access to customer data to improve model performance.Dimon’s remarks place him among a growing group of business leaders advocating modelmaxxing — choosing the right‑sized, cost‑efficient AI model rather than defaulting to the most powerful (and expensive) frontier systems. This trend is a direct response to tokenmaxxing, where companies overuse high‑cost AI tools like Claude, Codex and Cursor in ways that add little value.Palantir CEO Alex Karp has been one of the strongest critics of tokenmaxxing, saying AI models have been “oversold” and that many companies are wasting money on tokens that deliver no meaningful returns. He even compared compulsive AI usage to porn addiction, calling it "demastinatory" behavior inside enterprises. Cerebras Systems CEO Andrew Feldman echoed the sentiment, saying unlimited token budgets were “boneheaded from the get‑go. ” His analogy: “You don’t need a Ferrari to go to the grocery store… use a lower‑cost open‑source model.”In related news, Jamie Dimon recently offered some fresh insight into what he might do once he eventually steps down from his position. Dimon said that he is more likely to write a book or teach than pursue politics. Speaking to Axios in an interview, Dimon said that he would focus on doing business ‘with people I like’ and possibly explore media-related projects. Dimon also addressed the speculation that he could be headed for the White House, saying there is “pretty much no chance” he would run for office. “I’m very hard-pressed to think I should be doing something like that,” he said with a laugh, adding that he’s never been part of a campaign. The JPMorgan CEO cited his age (70) and past health issues including emergency heart surgery in 2020 and throat cancer in 2014, as reasons politics is unlikely.
Article Summary: Jamie dimon, ceo of america’s biggest bank says that the era of unchecked ai spending is over. Warns that businesses must treat ai ‘like any other resource’ as costs rise sharply. Dimon said ‘we are very protective of our data and ip’ in the age of generative ai.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
